verdict.rationale: Maritime documents automatic sleep when idle for served containers, and its CLI exposes a `timeLimitMinutes` setting (formerly `lifetimeMinutes`), which suggests a configurable time limit. Billing is flat per agent rather than metered, so stopping a sandbox does not reduce cost the way the story assumes. Missing for 10: documented semantics and configuration of idle-timeout values, clarity on what `timeLimitMinutes` applies to and what happens when it expires, any billing stop tied to shutdown, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can set timeouts so sandboxes shut down automatically and stop billing when idle or done

citations.quote: puts it to sleep when idle, and wakes it on the next visit.
a documented deprecated alias kept for old clients (`lifetimeMinutes` for `timeLimitMinutes` in the CLI docs)
No meters, no hourly rates: how much your agents run never changes the bill.
